name: Dark Rose
lede: Dark Rose is a deep, muted pinkish red, a modern descriptive name for a rose-toned crimson.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body:
Our earliest record of Dark Rose as a color name is the xkcd color list of 2010 [3]. The words themselves are far older. Pliny described the finest Tyrian purple as gleaming with the hue of a dark rose, a phrase Ball quotes in his chapter on dyes [1]. Gage adds that medieval writers such as Isidore of Seville and Bede used the same comparison for the amethyst [4].

That is a coincidence of words, not a lineage. Pliny meant a purple, and this swatch is a red-pink, so the old phrase and this modern name only share a vocabulary [1][4].

sections.title: Where it sits
sections.body: Its nearest neighbors among our names, by CIELAB distance, are [[popstar|Popstar]], [[pomegranate-purple|Pomegranate Purple]] and [[light-burgundy|Light Burgundy]] [5]. On a white page it reaches a contrast ratio of 5.19:1 [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Dark Rose appears in 11 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.05%, as photographed [6]. That makes it rarer than 73% of the named colors [6]. In printed English the phrase peaks in the 1900s, though that counts every use of the words, including the flower [6].
